column106: On 6 feb. 2022 4:42PM, according to the CTV news unofficial vaccine tracker, 31,999,377 Canadians (84% of the total national population and 88% of the vaccine-eligible population aged 5+) have received at least one dose of an approved COVID-19 vaccine -- Moderna, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson (J&J) Janssen, or AstraZeneca (no longer recommended except in limited circumstances).30,344,423 Canadians (79% of total pop. and 83.5% of vax-eligible aged 5+) have received two doses. All provinces and territories are making vaccinations available to residents aged 5 and up. Vaccinations for those aged 5-11 started in late November 2021. Provinces and territories are also delivering third doses to long-term care residents, immune-compromised patients, indigenous community residents, senior citizens and recipients of two earlier AZ doses based on national government guidance. The Government-of-Canada-recommended age for third doses has been lowered to those aged 50 and up and to age 18+ where local circumstances warrant. 16,254,970 third doses have been administered accounting for 42% of the national population. Some provinces have started delivering fourth doses. (Note that vaccination data do not include Canadians who returned home after being vaccinated in other countries while wintering at retirement homes or on essential work trips. On the other hand, there may be a small amount of double-counting when residents live and work in different provinces, vaccinations took place at work, and both provinces count the vaccinations.) “Free vaccines will be available to everyone in Canada.” See government of Canada and CTV news websites, archived:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220205194529/https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/diseases/coronavirus-disease-covid-19/vaccines.html  https://web.archive.org/web/20220205192553/https://health-infobase.canada.ca/covid-19/vaccination-coverage/  https://web.archive.org/web/20220207121217/https://www.ctvnews.ca/health/coronavirus/covid-19-vaccine-booster-eligibility-by-province-and-territory-in-canada  https://web.archive.org/web/20220107190826/https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/phac-aspc/documents/services/immunization/national-advisory-committee-on-immunization-naci/guidance-booster-covid-19-vaccine-doses/summary.pdf

column88: On 25 feb. 2022, the policy intent of some jurisdictions continues to   be to supplement polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of symptomatic cases with mass availability of lateral flow and other rapid tests to asymptomatic individuals. column106: On 7 march 2022 11:23AM, according to the CTV news unofficial vaccine tracker, 32,179,152 Canadians (84% of the total national population and 88.5% of the vaccine-eligible population aged 5+) have received at least one dose of an approved COVID-19 vaccine -- Moderna, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson (J&J) Janssen, or AstraZeneca (no longer recommended except in limited circumstances) and with Novavax and Medicago Cofifenz just approved, but not yet available. 30,965,820 Canadians (81% of total pop. and 85% of vax-eligible aged 5+) have received two doses. column106: On 11 march 2022 1:39PM EST, according to the CTV news unofficial vaccine tracker, 32,257,307 Canadians (84% of the total national population and 89% of the vaccine-eligible population aged 5+) have received at least one dose of an approved COVID-19 vaccine -- Moderna, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson (J&J) Janssen, or AstraZeneca (no longer recommended except in limited circumstances) and with Novavax and Medicago Cofifenz recently approved. 31,009,759 Canadians (81% of total pop. and 85% of vax-eligible aged 5+) have received two doses. All provinces and territories are making vaccinations available to residents aged 5 and up. Vaccinations for those aged 5-11 started in late November 2021. Provinces and territories are also delivering third doses to long-term care residents, immune-compromised patients, indigenous community residents, senior citizens and recipients of two earlier AZ doses based on national government guidance. The Government-of-Canada-recommended age for third doses has been lowered to those aged 50 and up, to age 18+ where local circumstances warrant and to age 12+ for immune-compromised patients as well as other specific circumstances. 17,753,457 third doses have been administered accounting for 46% of the national population. Some provinces have started delivering fourth doses and third doses to all those aged 12-17. (Note that vaccination data do not include Canadians who returned home after being vaccinated in other countries while wintering at retirement homes or on essential work trips. On the other hand, there may be a small amount of double-counting when residents live and work in different provinces, vaccinations took place at work, and both provinces count the vaccinations.) “Free vaccines will be available to everyone in Canada.” See government of Canada website, archived:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220311190227/https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/diseases/coronavirus-disease-covid-19/vaccines.html  https://web.archive.org/web/20220107190826/https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/phac-aspc/documents/services/immunization/national-advisory-committee-on-immunization-naci/guidance-booster-covid-19-vaccine-doses/summary.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20220225152737/https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/covid19-industry/drugs-vaccines-treatments/vaccines.html

column90: On 18 april 2022, government of Canada advises that when individuals “test positive for COVID-19, a public health official will ask you questions to collect important information about your symptoms; activities and travel you did before you tested positive; all the people you may have been in close contact with while you were contagious ...contact tracing. It's a key public health measure.” Most provinces and territories intend to follow this practice, if conditions and resources permit. However, tracing capacity is not sufficient in most jurisdictions to deal with high case numbers. In most cases, contact tracing responsibility is up to individuals who are symptomatic and/or have tested positive. In Canada’s most populous province Ontario: “If you have symptoms of COVID-19 or have tested positive, tell your close contacts that they have been exposed… Informing your contact will help stop the spread of the virus. Give them the link to this webpage, ontario.ca/exposed, so they can protect themselves and their contacts.” See Governments of Canada and Ontario websites, archived:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220418134725/https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/diseases/2019-novel-coronavirus-infection/symptoms/testing.html   https://web.archive.org/web/20220416122727/https://covid-19.ontario.ca/exposed

column106: On 18 april 2022 6:41PM EDT, according to the CTV news unofficial vaccine tracker, 32,564,647 Canadians (85% of the total national population and just under 90% of the vaccine-eligible population aged 5+) have received at least one dose of an approved COVID-19 vaccine -- Moderna, Pfizer, Johnson & Johnson (J&J) Janssen, or AstraZeneca (no longer recommended except in limited circumstances) and Novavax and Medicago Cofifenz recently approved. 31,227,198 Canadians (82% of total pop. and 86% of vax-eligible aged 5+) have received two doses. All provinces and territories are making vaccinations available to residents aged 5 and up. Provinces and territories are also delivering third doses. 18,296,347 third doses have been administered accounting for 48% of the national population. Provinces and territories have started delivering fourth doses in some circumstances. (Note that vaccination data may not include Canadians who returned home after being vaccinated in other countries while wintering at retirement homes or on essential work trips. column119: On 18 april 2022, eligibility continues to be 5 years of age and up in all provinces and territories consistent with national government guidance. In addition: “[National Advisory Committee on Immunization] NACI’s initial guidance on the use of second booster doses of COVID-19 vaccines will help provinces and territories decide on timing and prioritization for rollout of these immunization programs across different populations, based on local epidemiology and unique circumstances in their regions. Preliminary data indicate that a second booster dose of a COVID-19 vaccine can offer additional protection against infection, severe illness, hospitalization and death. At this time, we expect specific high-risk groups, including residents of long term care homes and seniors aged 80 years or over living in the community, to benefit the most from a second booster dose. column15: On 25 april 2022, some jurisdictions have no covid-related health measures in schools. However, some provinces and territories continue to require masks and other covid-related health measures in schools – e.g., some Atlantic provinces and Quebec. Some post-secondary institutions throughout Canada are offering classes and exams online or have implemented vaccine mandates for students and staff to enter campus. In most cases, these decisions are set by individual post-secondary institutions rather than dictated or guided by governments. E.g., “Ontario’s top doctor said … that vaccine policies at post-secondary institutions have served their purpose and should be dropped, saying their removal should align with the [1 March] end of the province’s vaccine certificate system. column119: On 16 may 2022, eligibility in all provinces and territories continues to be consistent with national government guidance – 5 years of age and up with no prioritization between groups for delivery of first doses. In addition: “[National Advisory Committee on Immunization] NACI’s initial guidance on the use of second booster doses of COVID-19 vaccines will help provinces and territories decide on timing and prioritization for rollout of these immunization programs across different populations, based on local epidemiology and unique circumstances in their regions. Preliminary data indicate that a second booster dose of a COVID-19 vaccine can offer additional protection against infection, severe illness, hospitalization and death. At this time, we expect specific high-risk groups, including residents of long term care homes and seniors aged 80 years or over living in the community, to benefit the most from a second booster dose. As NACI’s review continues, the recommendation stands for adults to receive a COVID-19 primary vaccine series and a first booster dose of an authorized mRNA vaccine… While the greatest benefit of second boosters are expected in long-term care, congregate living settings for seniors, and for those 80 years of age and older living in the community; jurisdictions may also choose to offer a second COVID-19 booster dose to adults 70 to 79 years of age living in the community.” See government of Canada website, archived:  https://web.archive.org/web/20220515162823/https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/diseases/coronavirus-disease-covid-19/vaccines.html  https://web.archive.org/web/20220515163212/https://health-infobase.canada.ca/covid-19/vaccination-coverage/  https://web.archive.org/web/20220424222620/https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/phac-aspc/documents/services/immunization/national-advisory-committee-on-immunization-naci/naci-summary-april-12-2022.pdf  https://web.archive.org/web/20220424224511/https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/covid19-industry/drugs-vaccines-treatments/vaccines.html

column69: On 11 July 2022, the government of Canada policy remains in place: “Vaccination requirements are suspended Proof of vaccination is no longer required to board a plane or train in Canada.” However: “To embark on a cruise ship that will start, dock or end in Canada, if you’re 12 years of age or older, you must be fully vaccinated against COVID-19”. There are some commercial domestic cruises solely within Canada. But, unvaccinated persons who wish to travel – e.g., from Quebec City to Montreal or a destination in Ontario – can now do so by air or rail, even if their first preference to travel by commercial boat cruise remains unavailable. For most consumers, the principal appeals of a commercial boat cruise – dining, accommodation and sightseeing – outweigh traveling from one city to another. The removal of the vaccine mandate for domestic air and rail passengers means that travel within Canada is open to both vaccinated and unvaccinated persons. column69: On 31 dec. 2022, the government of Canada policy remains in place: “proof of vaccination is no longer required to … board a plane or train in Canada. This applies to travel within Canada and flights or trains leaving Canada…Wearing masks on planes and trains in Canada is not required.” See Government of Canada website, archived:  https://web.archive.org/web/20221230111038/https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/diseases/coronavirus-disease-covid-19/vaccines/vaccine-proof.html  https://web.archive.org/web/20221228223443/https://travel.gc.ca/travel-covid
column74: As of 31 Dec. 2022, the government of Canada policy remains in place: “For all travellers entering Canada by air, land or marine mode on or after October 1, 2022:  Proof of COVID-19 vaccination is not required  COVID-19 pre-entry and arrival tests are not required  Quarantine after you enter Canada is not required  Using ArriveCAN is not required …  Pre-boarding tests for cruise passengers are not required …  Health checks to board planes and trains are not required  Wearing masks on planes and trains is not required … If you have symptoms of COVID-19, you shouldn't travel to Canada.” (The last point is a recommendation for voluntary compliance, not a mandatory restriction.) However, “on January 5, [2023] all air travellers who are two years of age and older, arriving on flights originating from the People’s Republic of China, Hong Kong or Macao, will need to provide evidence of a negative COVID-19 test result, taken no more than two days before their departure, to the airline prior to boarding. The test could be either a negative molecular (such as a PCR test), or a negative antigen test that has documentation to show that it has been monitored by a telehealth service or an accredited laboratory or testing provider. Passengers who tested positive more than 10 days before their departure flight, but no more than 90 days, can provide the airline with documentation of their prior positive, in place of a negative test result.” See Government of Canada websites, archived:   https://web.archive.org/web/20221228223443/travel.gc.ca/travel-covid  https://web.archive.org/web/20230101032521/https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/news/2022/12/government-of-canada-announces-negative-covid-19-test-requirement-for-travellers-arriving-from-the-peoples-republic-of-china-hong-kong-or-macao-air.html  https://web.archive.org/web/20220926181459/https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/news/2022/09/government-of-canada-to-remove-covid-19-border-and-travel-measures-effective-october-1.html

column79: On 31 Dec. 2022, the statement on Finance Canada’s website continues: “To help students and young Canadians who have been particularly hard-hit by COVID-19, we are waiving the interest for full-time and part-time students on the federal portion of Canada Student Loans and Canada Apprentice Loans until March 31, 2023.” However, on 3 Nov. 2022, the government of Canada’s Minister of Finance announced “new, targeted cost of living support measures to make life more affordable for the Canadians most affected by rising prices…With life becoming more expensive for many recent graduates, the government is taking new, permanent steps to reduce the burden of student loans on young Canadians so they can invest in building their futures…the federal portion of all Canada Student Loans and Canada Apprentice Loans permanently interest-free, including those currently being repaid.” The decision to make the interest-free student loan policy permanent (until and unless a future government revokes the policy) as cost-of-living support indicates that this last vestige of covid support for borrowers is now based on other considerations not related to covid impact. See Government of Canada website, archived:  https://web.archive.org/web/20221107153355/https://www.canada.ca/en/department-finance/news/2022/11/making-life-more-affordable.html  https://web.archive.org/web/20221225114306/www.canada.ca/en/department-finance/economic-response-plan.html
column86: On 31 dec. 2022, the national government’s “urges caution” stance continues stressing individual responsibility for managing risk. “Governments and public health authorities across Canada continue to adjust their public health advice based on their local situations. This includes easing of public health requirements. For this reason, you'll need to make your own decisions about which personal measures to take to reduce your risks.” Most sub-national governments have shifted to a “living with covid” approach with lower-profile and/or less frequent public communication emphasizing individual responsibility for risk management. column88: On 31 dec. 2022, the previous policy ideal to supplement polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of symptomatic cases with mass availability of lateral flow rapid tests to asymptomatic individuals (with tracking of positive tests) has been largely shelved. In most parts of Canada, the 2022 caseload wave continues to frustrate efforts to achieve testing aspirations as explained by the government of Canada: “the highly contagious Omicron variant caused a rapid increase in cases. This surge affected public health and testing capacity, which led to a change in testing strategies … This made it harder for provinces and territories to link cases. As a result, outbreaks were undercounted. The provinces and territories still consistently report cases of COVID-19 in high-priority settings …Acute care: Hospital or similar setting …Congregate living …Correctional facilities …Long-term care facilities”. E.g., “Testing … in Ontario was restricted to high-risk populations and settings in January 2022.… If you are at higher risk of severe outcomes of COVID-19, you are eligible for PCR or rapid molecular testing and should seek out testing as soon as possible if you develop symptoms.” See Governments of Canada and Ontario websites, archived:  https://web.archive.org/web/20221230130711/https://health-infobase.canada.ca/covid-19/outbreaks.html  https://web.archive.org/web/20221230133429/https://www.publichealthontario.ca/-/media/Documents/nCoV/epi/covid-19-weekly-epi-summary-report.pdf?sc_lang=en  https://web.archive.org/web/20221228232335/https://www.ontario.ca/page/covid-19-testing-and-treatment

column94: On 31 Dec. 2022, there is some doubt about whether all of the C$8 billion = US$6,393 million amount budgeted for buying covid vaccines and recorded on 14Apr2021 has actually been spent.
